Implementer notes (Claude Opus 5.5, the lead). Use them as context only; the judgment is yours.

Scope: spec `pose-review-resume-keeps-the-sealed-checkout` (R1–R3, decision D1, accepted limits L1–L2). On 2026-11-25 a `pose delegate resume` started a new run whose resumed Codex session still referred to the first attempt's sealed checkout, which the interrupted run's cleanup had removed; the reviewer stopped and the resume produced nothing.
- R1: every run of an attempt now uses the same runtime directory, `pose-review-run-<first 32 hex of the attempt id>` under the temporary directory (`reviewRunRuntimeDir` in `pose-mcp/internal/pose/review_dispatch.go`), so the checkout is recreated at the path the session saw. A run without an attempt keeps a random name.
- R2: `TestResumedReviewFindsItsSealedCheckoutAtTheSamePath` (internal/cli) records the first run's working directory, checks it was removed, and resumes with an adapter that fails unless it runs there.
- R3: the directory is created with `os.Mkdir`; an existing path or a link fails the run with its reason (`TestTheAttemptRuntimeDirectoryIsCreatedExclusively`).
Each test fails with its guard mutated out. D1 explains why the path is kept stable instead of telling the session a new one (the continuation sends the sealed brief, whose wire digest provenance checks).

Please check in particular that no run can share or follow a directory it did not create, that cleanup still removes the whole runtime directory, and that runs outside an attempt behave as before.

Before you finish, run `"$POSE_REVIEW_CLI" review draft-check --draft -` on your final message (pipe it on standard input) and fix every reason it reports.

Draft format rules, enforced by the conclusion preflight:
- New findings use short unprefixed IDs (N1, N2, …).
- Structural-delta mappings go inside the criterion that answers them, with `basis` set to a requirement or a decision of this spec (R1–R3, D1).
- A criterion scoped to a component cites evidence from that component only.
- A finding that falls inside an accepted limit (L1, L2) is a follow-up with `limit` set to its id.

Sandbox limits: the checkout is sealed and read-only. Never `cd`; keep the checkout root as the working directory. Your Bash is limited to these command prefixes: `go test`, `go vet`, `go -C`, `git diff|log|show|status|ls-files`, `cat`, `printf`, `"$POSE_REVIEW_CLI"`, and the pose checks the plan lists. Keep test runs focused (`go -C pose-mcp test ./internal/cli ./internal/pose -run 'RunContinuity|ResumedReview|AttemptRuntimeDirectory'`, `go -C pose-mcp vet ./internal/cli ./internal/pose`), and let every command you start finish before you end. Run every planned `pose` command as `"$POSE_REVIEW_CLI"`. A tool you cannot rerun in the sandbox is a limit of the run, not a defect of the subject: cite the sealed evidence that covers it.

Please report every finding you see in this round, classified blocker or follow-up, rather than stopping at the first.

Round 2 notes: round 1 (rrn-7adbffa551b9acf2) ended without a draft because the reviewer's Bash sandbox failed to start ("Failed to create bridge sockets"); the cause is found and fixed (see round 4 notes). From its reading-only findings: N1, `PlanReviewResume` now refuses a leftover runtime directory before the continuation is claimed (`reviewRunRuntimeDirFree`), so removing it restores the resume; N2, the R2 adapter exits unless the recreated checkout holds the spec; N3, the manual in both locales states the stable path, the `TMPDIR` condition and the remedy; N4, a run that fails right after creating the directory removes it; N5 is declared as accepted limit L3.

Round 3 notes: round 2 (rrn-c5d57ff07d69ec1a) requested changes. N7: the manual, the spec's technical risks and both messages now say the remedy applies to a directory present although the last run cleaned up; a predecessor whose cleanup did not complete is refused as before. N6: `PlanReviewHandoff` checks the directory before it claims the run. N9: the regression tests are renamed `TestRunContinuity…` so the matrix's `RunContinuity` pattern runs them. N10: the exclusivity test sets `TMP` and `TEMP` too. N8 is recorded as a spec follow-up. Also, between rounds the full suite showed a repeated resume refused beside the directory: the check now runs only for a continuation still to start.

Round 4 notes: rounds 1 and 3 lost Bash because of this spec itself: the reviewer's `TMPDIR` is the run's runtime directory, and the 32-hex name made it 70 bytes, so the Claude sandbox's Unix socket paths under it passed the ~108-byte bound. The name now has 10 hex digits, as long as the random one it replaced, with a test. Your Bash should now work: please run the required tools (`artifact-check`, `surface-check`, the validate tools) and record them `passed` with their evidence, as the brief says. Round 3 (rrn-95a0d363d2041e1d) approved with N11–N15 as follow-ups, but its conclusion was refused for the deferred tools; its findings are therefore not in the ledger. Please re-examine them and record any that still hold, with action, owner and review_by.

Round 5 notes: round 4 (rrn-17b88c930fddf599) requested changes. N16: the length test now compares with the longest random name (prefix plus ten digits) and passed 300 repeated runs; the comment says the same. N19: the handoff refusal ends "then hand off again". N20: the link case is skipped, with a log line, where a link cannot be created. N17, N18 and N21 are recorded as spec follow-ups.
